answer: Make reward weight depend on reciprocal bandwidth reservations. Each identity leases a 2-Mbps path from four unrelated relays for 14 days and posts a 30-POA service bond. A mesa beacon chooses six surprise one-minute tests daily; five auditors verify signed packet traces. The ferrous rule rejects paths sharing an upstream /24, while a public trellis maps relay ancestry. N aliases therefore need 8N Mbps-days and lock 30N POA; two failed tests burn that identity bond.
